paragraphs.paragraph: These verses summarize the territories of Sihon and Og, their defeat by Moses and the Israelites, and the granting of their land as an inheritance to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh.
paragraphs.title: Summary of the Conquest East of the Jordan

easy.explanation: The passage describes the land on the other side of Jordan toward the rising of the sun.
easy.q: Where were the territories described at the beginning of the passage located?

answers: Joshua and the king of Jericho
Pharaoh and the king of Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The passage names Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan.
easy.q: Who were the two main kings mentioned in the conquest east of the Jordan?

answers: To the tribe of Judah alone
To all the kings of the land
To the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh
easy.explanation: Moses gave the land for a possession to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh.
easy.q: To whom was the conquered land given as a possession?

answers: From Aroer by the river Arnon to the river Jabbok
From the wilderness to the south country
medium.explanation: Sihon ruled from Aroer on the bank of the river Arnon to the river Jabbok.
medium.q: What boundary is given for the territory ruled by Sihon?

answers: Land given to be owned or inherited
medium.explanation: A possession is something given to someone to own, especially land given as an inheritance.
medium.q: In the KJV passage, what does the word "possession" mean?

answers: After the kings were defeated, Moses gave their land as a possession to certain tribes
The land was divided among the kings before they were defeated
The land was returned to Sihon and Og after the battle
medium.explanation: The passage connects the defeat of the kings with Moses giving their land to the Israelite tribes.
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between defeating Sihon and Og and dividing the land?

challenge.explanation: The passage calls Og the king of Bashan.
challenge.q: Which king ruled in Bashan according to the passage?

answers: The territory is described in detailed geographical terms
The kings ruled over no territory
The verses discuss only the names of the Israelites
challenge.explanation: The passage names rivers, mountains, plains, seas, and borders to describe the territories.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the many boundaries listed in these verses?

answers: All of the tribe of Manasseh
challenge.explanation: The passage specifically says that half the tribe of Manasseh received the land.
challenge.q: What portion of Manasseh received an inheritance east of the Jordan?

paragraphs.idea: These verses summarize the territories of Sihon and Og, their defeat by Moses and the Israelites, and the granting of their land as an inheritance to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh.

paragraphs.paragraph: These verses begin the list of kings defeated by Joshua and the Israelites west of the Jordan and describe the regions of the land and the peoples who had previously lived there.
paragraphs.title: Summary of the Conquest West of the Jordan

easy.explanation: The passage says that Joshua and the children of Israel smote these kings on the west side of Jordan.
easy.q: Who defeated the kings west of the Jordan?

answers: A list of the kings of the land
A list of the tribes of Israel
A description of the exodus from Egypt
easy.explanation: The verses begin the list of kings whom Joshua and Israel defeated.
The passage mentions the mountains, valleys, plains, springs, wilderness, and south country.
easy.q: Which of the following regions is named in the passage?

answers: From Baal-gad in the valley of Lebanon to mount Halak, which goes up to Seir
From the river Arnon to mount Hermon
medium.explanation: Joshua 12:7 gives this as the extent of the land west of Jordan.
medium.q: Between which places is the conquered land described?

answers: According to the portions or divisions assigned to the tribes
According to the number of kings
According to the height of the mountains
medium.explanation: Joshua gave the land to the tribes of Israel according to the divisions or portions assigned to them.
medium.q: In context, what does "according to their divisions" mean?

answers: They were peoples who had previously lived in the land
They were peoples who received the land from Joshua
They were peoples who lived only east of the Jordan
medium.explanation: The passage lists the peoples who had lived in the various regions of the land.
medium.q: What do the verses say about the peoples in the land?

answers: The first section concerns the land east of Jordan, while the second concerns the land west of Jordan
The first section concerns only northern kings, while the second concerns only southern kings
The first section concerns peoples, while the second concerns only rivers
challenge.explanation: Verses 1–6 summarize the defeat of Sihon and Og east of Jordan, while verses 7–8 begin the account of the land west of Jordan.
challenge.q: What is the main difference between verses 1–6 and verses 7–8?

answers: Mountains, valleys, plains, springs, wilderness, and south country
challenge.explanation: This is the order in which the regions are listed in the KJV.
challenge.q: Which sequence presents the regions named in verse 8?

challenge.explanation: The passage names the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
challenge.q: Which of the following peoples is named in the passage?

paragraphs.idea: These verses begin the list of kings defeated by Joshua and the Israelites west of the Jordan and describe the regions of the land and the peoples who had previously lived there.

paragraphs.paragraph: These verses list many defeated kings, beginning with the kings of Jericho and Ai, continuing through the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, the lowland and southern cities, and ending with the kings of Tappuah, Hepher, Aphek, and Lasharon.
paragraphs.title: The First Group of Defeated Kings

easy.explanation: The list begins with the king of Jericho.
easy.q: Which king appears first in the list?

easy.explanation: The verse lists the king of Jerusalem and the king of Hebron together.
easy.q: Which king is listed beside the king of Jerusalem?

answers: The king of Tappuah and the king of Hepher
The king of Jericho and the king of Ai
The king of Madon and the king of Hazor
easy.explanation: Verse 18 names the king of Tappuah and the king of Hepher.
easy.q: Which two kings are named in verse 18?

answers: Two kings are named, and each is followed by the word "one"
One king is named beside a tribe
One city is named beside a river
medium.explanation: The list repeatedly names two kings and states that each was one.
medium.q: What repeated pattern appears through most of the list?

medium.explanation: Verse 9 names the king of Jericho and the king of Ai, followed by verse 10's kings of Jerusalem and Hebron.
medium.q: Which pair belongs to the list in verses 9–10?

answers: From early cities such as Jericho and Ai to many additional cities and regions
From the north only to the east side of Jordan
medium.explanation: The list begins with Jericho and Ai and continues through many other cities and places.
medium.q: How does the list progress from verse 9 through verse 18?

challenge.explanation: The KJV says, "The king of Ai, which is beside Bethel."
challenge.q: Which king is described as being beside Bethel?

challenge.explanation: Aphek and Lasharon appear in verse 18, but Megiddo appears later, in verse 21.
challenge.q: Which of the following names does not appear in verses 9–18?

answers: All the cities were equal in size
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording counts each named king as one individual king.
challenge.q: What does the repeated word "one" show in this list?

paragraphs.idea: These verses list many defeated kings, beginning with the kings of Jericho and Ai, continuing through the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, the lowland and southern cities, and ending with the kings of Tappuah, Hepher, Aphek, and Lasharon.

paragraphs.paragraph: These verses complete the list with the kings of Madon, Hazor, Shimron-meron, Achshaph, Taanach, Megiddo, Kedesh, Jokneam, Dor, the nations at Gilgal, and Tirzah, ending with the total of thirty-one kings.
paragraphs.title: The Northern Kings and the Final Count

easy.explanation: Verse 19 begins with the king of Madon.

answers: The king of Taanach and the king of Megiddo
The king of Madon and the king of Hazor
The king of Dor and the king of Tirzah
easy.explanation: Verse 21 names the king of Taanach and the king of Megiddo.
easy.q: Which pair of kings is named in verse 21?

easy.explanation: The final verse says, "all the kings thirty and one."
easy.q: How many kings were counted altogether?

answers: The king of Shimron-meron and the king of Achshaph
The king of Kedesh and the king of Jokneam
The king of Dor and the king of the nations
medium.explanation: Verse 20 names the king of Shimron-meron and the king of Achshaph.
The passage names the king of Jokneam of Carmel.
medium.q: Which king is associated with Carmel?

answers: Madon and Hazor, Shimron-meron and Achshaph, Taanach and Megiddo
Hazor and Madon, Megiddo and Taanach, Achshaph and Shimron-meron
Tirzah and Dor, Madon and Hazor, Kedesh and Jokneam
medium.explanation: This is the order in which the pairs appear in verses 19–21.
medium.q: Which order of pairs is correct?

challenge.explanation: Verse 24 names the king of Tirzah immediately before giving the total.
challenge.q: Which name appears near the end of the list, just before the final count?

answers: It gives the total number of kings
It begins the conquest east of Jordan
It describes the boundaries of Sihon's kingdom
challenge.explanation: The final verse concludes the list by giving the total of thirty-one kings.
challenge.q: What is the function of verse 24 in relation to the preceding verses?

challenge.explanation: The KJV says, "The king of Dor in the coast of Dor."
challenge.q: Which name appears with the phrase "in the coast of Dor"?

paragraphs.idea: These verses complete the list with the kings of Madon, Hazor, Shimron-meron, Achshaph, Taanach, Megiddo, Kedesh, Jokneam, Dor, the nations at Gilgal, and Tirzah, ending with the total of thirty-one kings.
